Nimbus Logistics IT Handbook

# Nimbus Logistics Pvt. Ltd. — IT Handbook

**Document Owner:** IT Department
**Version:** 2.4
**Effective Date:** 1 October 2026
**Applies To:** All employees, contractors, and interns

> This is a sample document for a fictional company, created for illustration and template purposes.

---

Nimbus Logistics IT Handbook > 1. Welcome and Purpose

Nimbus Logistics Pvt. Ltd. is a Mumbai-headquartered supply chain and freight-tech company with offices in Mumbai, Pune, and Bengaluru, and a warehouse network across India.

This handbook explains how technology is provided, used, and protected at Nimbus. It helps you:

- Get set up quickly in your first week
- Know what you can and cannot do with company systems
- Keep company and customer data safe
- Get help fast when something breaks

**Our IT principles**

| Principle | What it means |
|---|---|
| Secure by default | Security controls are on unless there is an approved reason to turn them off |
| Least privilege | You get the access you need for your role, and no more |
| Self-service first | Common tasks should be doable without raising a ticket |
| One source of truth | Tools, assets, and documentation live in approved systems only |

---

Nimbus Logistics IT Handbook > 2. Getting Started: Onboarding

### 2.1 Before Day 1

IT prepares the following once HR confirms your joining date:

- Corporate email account and directory profile
- Laptop, imaged and encrypted
- Role-based access groups (see Section 3)
- Welcome email with your temporary credentials and joining instructions

### 2.2 Day 1 Checklist

- [ ] Collect your laptop and accessories from the IT desk (or courier, for remote hires)
- [ ] Sign the Equipment Acknowledgement Form
- [ ] Log in and change your temporary password
- [ ] Enrol in Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
- [ ] Install the Nimbus VPN client from the Software Portal
- [ ] Join the `#it-help` channel on Slack
- [ ] Complete the mandatory Security Awareness training (within 7 days)

### 2.3 First-Week Tools

| Tool | Purpose | How to access |
|---|---|---|
| Nimbus Mail | Email and calendar | mail.nimbus-logistics.example |
| Slack | Team chat | Desktop or mobile app |
| Zoom | Video meetings | Software Portal |
| Jira | Tickets and project tracking | jira.nimbus-logistics.example |
| Confluence | Documentation | wiki.nimbus-logistics.example |
| HR Portal | Payslips, leave, policies | hr.nimbus-logistics.example |
| Software Portal | Approved software installs | Self-service app on laptop |

---

Nimbus Logistics IT Handbook > 3. Accounts and Access Management

### 3.1 Account Types

- **Standard account:** Issued to every employee, tied to a single named individual.
- **Privileged account:** For administrators only, issued separately and monitored.
- **Service account:** For applications and automation, owned by a named team.
- **Guest account:** For visitors and short-term vendors, limited to 30 days.

### 3.2 Requesting Access

1. Raise an **Access Request** ticket in the Service Desk.
2. Specify the system, access level, and business justification.
3. Your manager approves; for sensitive systems, the system owner also approves.
4. IT provisions access within **2 business days**.

### 3.3 Access Reviews

Managers review team access every quarter. Access that is no longer needed is removed. Accounts unused for 90 days are automatically disabled.

### 3.4 Rules

- Never share your account with anyone, including your manager or IT staff.
- Do not use another person's credentials, even if offered.
- Privileged access must be requested separately and expires after 12 months unless renewed.

---

Nimbus Logistics IT Handbook > 4. Passwords and Authentication

### 4.1 Password Requirements

| Requirement | Standard |
|---|---|
| Minimum length | 14 characters |
| Complexity | Passphrases recommended (e.g., four unrelated words) |
| Reuse | Cannot reuse your last 10 passwords |
| Expiry | Every 365 days, or immediately if compromise is suspected |
| Lockout | 5 failed attempts locks the account for 15 minutes |

### 4.2 Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)

MFA is **mandatory** for email, VPN, cloud consoles, and all admin systems.

- **Preferred:** Authenticator app (push or one-time code)
- **Backup:** Hardware security key (issued on request)
- **Not allowed for privileged accounts:** SMS codes

### 4.3 Password Manager

Nimbus provides a company password manager. Use it to generate and store unique passwords for every work system. Do not store passwords in spreadsheets, notes apps, or browsers.

### 4.4 If You Forget Your Password

Use the self-service reset at `reset.nimbus-logistics.example`. If you are locked out of MFA, contact the Service Desk with ID verification.

---

Nimbus Logistics IT Handbook > 5. Hardware and Equipment

### 5.1 Standard Issue

| Role | Device | Accessories |
|---|---|---|
| Engineering | 16" laptop, 32 GB RAM | Monitor, keyboard, mouse, headset |
| Operations / Business | 14" laptop, 16 GB RAM | Mouse, headset |
| Warehouse supervisors | Rugged tablet | Scanner, protective case |

### 5.2 Your Responsibilities

- Keep devices physically secure; never leave them unattended in public or in a vehicle.
- Do not remove or disable disk encryption, antivirus, or the endpoint management agent.
- Report loss or theft **within 1 hour** (see Section 13).
- Return all equipment on exit (see Section 15).

### 5.3 Refresh Cycle

Laptops are refreshed every **4 years**. Earlier replacement is available for hardware faults. Request via the Service Desk.

### 5.4 Personal Peripherals

Personal keyboards, mice, and monitors are fine. Personal USB storage devices are **blocked** by default. Request an exception if you have a legitimate need.

---

Nimbus Logistics IT Handbook > 6. Software and Licensing

### 6.1 Approved Software

Install software only from the **Software Portal**. It contains pre-approved, licensed, and security-reviewed applications.

### 6.2 Requesting New Software

1. Search the Software Portal first.
2. If not listed, raise a **Software Request** with the business need.
3. IT and Security review for licensing, cost, and risk (typically 5 business days).

### 6.3 Not Allowed

- Pirated or cracked software
- Unapproved file-sharing or remote-access tools
- Browser extensions that read all page data without approval
- Cryptocurrency miners or similar software

### 6.4 Developer Tools

Engineers may install IDEs, language runtimes, and containers from approved sources. Open-source dependencies must pass the automated licence and vulnerability scan in CI before release.

### 6.5 AI Tools

Use only AI assistants approved by Nimbus. Do **not** paste customer data, credentials, source code marked Confidential, or contract details into unapproved AI tools. See the AI Usage Guideline on Confluence for the approved list.

---

Nimbus Logistics IT Handbook > 7. Network, Wi-Fi, and VPN

### 7.1 Office Wi-Fi

| Network | Who | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Nimbus-Corp` | Employees | Company devices only; certificate-based |
| `Nimbus-Guest` | Visitors | Internet only; password changes weekly |
| `Nimbus-IoT` | Scanners, printers | Managed by IT; do not connect personal devices |

### 7.2 VPN

Use the company VPN whenever you access internal systems from outside an office. Do not disable it while working. Split tunnelling is not permitted for production access.

### 7.3 Public Networks

Avoid public Wi-Fi where possible. If you must use it, connect to the VPN first.

### 7.4 Network Rules

- Do not connect unapproved routers, switches, or access points.
- Do not scan or probe the network unless you are authorised by Security.
- Do not bypass web filtering.

---

Nimbus Logistics IT Handbook > 8. Email and Collaboration Tools

### 8.1 Email

- Use your company email for all work communication.
- Do not auto-forward work email to personal accounts.
- Be cautious with attachments and links; see the phishing guidance in Section 9.4.
- Mailbox size limit: 50 GB. Retention rules are in Section 12.

### 8.2 Slack

- Use public channels by default; use private channels or DMs only when needed.
- Do not share passwords, keys, or customer personal data in Slack.
- Customer data may be shared only in channels approved for that purpose.

### 8.3 Video Meetings

- Use waiting rooms for external meetings.
- Do not record meetings without informing participants.
- Do not share meeting links publicly.

### 8.4 File Sharing

Store work files in the company cloud drive. Share by link with named people, not "anyone with the link". External sharing of Confidential or Restricted files needs manager approval.

---

Nimbus Logistics IT Handbook > 9. Information Security Policy

### 9.1 Data Classification

| Level | Description | Examples | Handling |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Public** | Approved for anyone | Marketing material, job posts | No restrictions |
| **Internal** | For employees only | Org charts, internal wikis | Do not share externally |
| **Confidential** | Business sensitive | Contracts, pricing, source code | Need-to-know; encrypted in transit and at rest |
| **Restricted** | Highest sensitivity | Customer personal data, credentials, financial records | Strict access control; logged; no local copies |

### 9.2 Core Rules

- Lock your screen when you step away (`Win + L` or `Ctrl + Cmd + Q`).
- Do not store Restricted data on laptops, phones, or personal storage.
- Use encrypted channels only (HTTPS, SFTP, VPN).
- Dispose of printed Confidential material by shredding.

### 9.3 Secure Development Basics

- Never commit secrets (API keys, tokens, passwords) to code repositories.
- Use the secrets manager for credentials.
- Code that handles Restricted data requires a security review before release.
- Dependencies are scanned automatically; critical findings must be fixed before deployment.

### 9.4 Spotting Phishing

Be suspicious of messages that:

- Create urgency ("pay now", "account will be closed")
- Ask for credentials, OTPs, or gift cards
- Come from a lookalike domain or unexpected sender
- Contain unexpected attachments or shortened links

Nimbus Logistics IT Handbook > 9. Information Security Policy

**What to do:** Do not click. Use the **Report Phish** button in your mail client, or forward to `security@nimbus-logistics.example`.

### 9.5 Physical Security

- Wear your ID badge visibly in the office.
- Do not let unknown people follow you through access-controlled doors.
- Escort visitors at all times.

---

Nimbus Logistics IT Handbook > 10. Acceptable Use Policy

### 10.1 Permitted Use

Company systems are provided for business use. Limited, reasonable personal use is allowed if it does not affect work, security, or company reputation.

### 10.2 Prohibited Activities

- Accessing, storing, or sharing illegal, offensive, or discriminatory content
- Harassing or threatening others using company systems
- Attempting to gain access to systems or data you are not authorised for
- Installing malware or deliberately disrupting services
- Using company systems for personal business or political campaigns
- Violating copyright or software licensing terms

### 10.3 Monitoring

Nimbus may monitor use of company systems, including email, web traffic, and device activity, to protect security and ensure compliance, consistent with applicable Indian law and the Company Privacy Notice.

### 10.4 Consequences

Violations may lead to access suspension, disciplinary action, or termination, and in serious cases, legal action.

---

Nimbus Logistics IT Handbook > 11. Remote Work and BYOD

### 11.1 Working Remotely

- Use a company laptop and the VPN.
- Work from a private location where screens cannot be seen by others.
- Do not use shared or public computers for work.
- Keep home Wi-Fi secured with WPA2/WPA3 and a strong password.

### 11.2 Bring Your Own Device (BYOD)

Personal phones and tablets may access email, Slack, and calendar only, under these conditions:

| Requirement | Detail |
|---|---|
| Enrolment | Install the Mobile Device Management (MDM) work profile |
| Screen lock | PIN, fingerprint, or face unlock required |
| OS updates | Supported, up-to-date OS version |
| Jailbroken or rooted devices | Not permitted |
| Lost device | Report within 1 hour; IT may remotely wipe the **work profile only** |

Personal laptops may **not** be used to access Confidential or Restricted data.

### 11.3 Working from Abroad

Notify your manager and IT before working outside India. Some countries have restrictions on encryption or data access, and access from certain regions may be blocked.

---

Nimbus Logistics IT Handbook > 12. Data Backup and Retention

### 12.1 Backups

| Data | Backup frequency | Retention |
|---|---|---|
| Production databases | Continuous + daily snapshot | 35 days |
| File shares and cloud drive | Daily | 90 days |
| Email | Continuous | 7 years (legal hold applies) |
| Laptops | **Not backed up** | Store work files in the cloud drive |

### 12.2 Your Responsibility

Save work to the cloud drive, not only to your local disk. If your laptop fails, files stored only locally may be lost.

### 12.3 Retention Rules

- Retain business records per the Records Retention Schedule (HR portal).
- Do not delete data that is subject to a legal hold, even if the schedule would otherwise allow it.
- Request restoration of deleted files via the Service Desk within the retention window.

---

Nimbus Logistics IT Handbook > 13. Incident Reporting

### 13.1 What Counts as an Incident

- Lost or stolen device
- Suspected phishing or malware
- Unauthorised access to an account or system
- Accidental sharing of Confidential or Restricted data
- Unusual system behaviour (ransom notes, unexpected pop-ups, locked files)

### 13.2 How to Report

| Urgency | Action | Time limit |
|---|---|---|
| **Critical** (data breach, ransomware, lost device with data) | Call the Security Hotline: **+91-22-5555-0199** (24x7) | Immediately, within 1 hour |
| **High / Medium** | Email `security@nimbus-logistics.example` or raise a Security Incident ticket | Same day |
| **Low** (suspicious email) | Use **Report Phish** button | When noticed |

### 13.3 What to Do While Waiting

1. Disconnect from the network if you suspect malware (turn off Wi-Fi; do not shut down).
2. Do not delete anything or try to "fix" it yourself.
3. Write down what happened and when.
4. Follow instructions from the Security team.

### 13.4 No-Blame Reporting

Report quickly and honestly. Nimbus encourages early reporting and does not penalise good-faith mistakes reported promptly.

---

Nimbus Logistics IT Handbook > 14. IT Support and Service Desk

### 14.1 Contact Options

| Channel | Details | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| Service Portal | support.nimbus-logistics.example | Tickets, requests, tracking |
| Email | `itsupport@nimbus-logistics.example` | Non-urgent issues |
| Slack | `#it-help` | Quick questions |
| Phone | +91-22-5555-0100 | Urgent issues |
| Walk-up desk | Mumbai HQ, 3rd Floor | Hardware, in person |

**Support hours:** Monday to Friday, 9:00 AM to 7:00 PM IST. After-hours support for Critical issues only, via the Security or On-Call hotline.

### 14.2 Priority and Response Targets

| Priority | Definition | Response | Target resolution |
|---|---|---|---|
| **P1 Critical** | Business-wide outage or security breach | 15 minutes | 4 hours |
| **P2 High** | Major function down for a team | 1 hour | 8 hours |
| **P3 Medium** | Single user issue, workaround exists | 4 hours | 3 business days |
| **P4 Low** | Request, question, minor issue | 1 business day | 5 business days |

### 14.3 Tips for a Faster Resolution

- Describe the problem and what you were doing when it happened.
- Include screenshots and exact error messages.
- Mention your device name (found in **Settings > About**).
- One issue per ticket.

### 14.4 Common Self-Service Fixes

Nimbus Logistics IT Handbook > 14. IT Support and Service Desk

| Problem | Try this first |
|---|---|
| Slow laptop | Restart; close unused apps; check for pending updates |
| Can't connect to VPN | Check internet; restart VPN client; verify MFA |
| Can't print | Confirm you are on `Nimbus-Corp`; re-add printer from Software Portal |
| Locked out | Use the self-service password reset |
| Meeting audio issues | Check Zoom audio settings; try a headset |

---

Nimbus Logistics IT Handbook > 15. Offboarding

### 15.1 Your Last Week

- Transfer ownership of files, repositories, and shared documents to your manager or a named colleague.
- Return all company equipment and accessories (laptop, charger, badge, security keys, scanners).
- Remove company data from any personal devices.

### 15.2 On Your Last Day

IT will:

- Disable your accounts and revoke VPN and MFA access
- Remove you from groups and shared channels
- Wipe the work profile from any enrolled personal device
- Forward your email to your manager for 30 days (when applicable)

### 15.3 After You Leave

Your mailbox and files are retained per the Retention Schedule. You must not access or retain any Nimbus data after your last day.

---

Nimbus Logistics IT Handbook > 16. FAQ

**Can I install Chrome extensions?**
Only those listed in the Software Portal. Request others via a Software Request.

**Can I use my personal laptop for work?**
No for Confidential or Restricted data. Personal phones can access email and Slack via MDM.

**I got a suspicious email. What should I do?**
Do not click anything. Use **Report Phish** or forward it to `security@nimbus-logistics.example`.

**How long does a new laptop take?**
Standard requests take 5 business days. Urgent replacements for faults are prioritised.

**Can I connect my own USB drive?**
USB storage is blocked by default. Raise an exception request with a business justification.

**Can I use ChatGPT or other AI tools with work data?**
Only approved AI tools, and never with Confidential or Restricted data in unapproved tools.

**Who do I contact if I lose my laptop on a weekend?**
Call the Security Hotline at +91-22-5555-0199 immediately.

---

Nimbus Logistics IT Handbook > 17. Appendix: Quick Reference

### Key Contacts

| Team | Contact |
|---|---|
| IT Service Desk | +91-22-5555-0100 / `itsupport@nimbus-logistics.example` |
| Security Hotline (24x7) | +91-22-5555-0199 |
| Security Team | `security@nimbus-logistics.example` |
| HR Helpdesk | `hr@nimbus-logistics.example` |

### Golden Rules

1. **Lock your screen** when you walk away.
2. **Use MFA** everywhere it is offered.
3. **Think before you click.** Report anything suspicious.
4. **Keep Restricted data** off laptops and personal tools.
5. **Report incidents fast**, within one hour for anything serious.
6. **Use only approved software and AI tools.**

# IT Policy Addendum, October 2026

This addendum updates specific sections of the IT Handbook (v2.4). Where this addendum and the handbook differ, **this addendum applies** from the effective date given in each item.

IT Policy Addendum, October 2026 > 1. Password expiry (effective 15 October 2026)

To reduce the risk of credential reuse, password expiry changes from every 365 days to every **180 days**. All other password requirements (14 characters minimum, no reuse of the last 10 passwords, lockout after 5 failed attempts) are unchanged. Users will receive a reminder 14 days before expiry.

IT Policy Addendum, October 2026 > 2. Extended support hours (effective 1 November 2026)

IT Service Desk hours extend to **Monday to Saturday, 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM IST**. Until 1 November 2026, existing hours (Monday to Friday, 9:00 AM to 7:00 PM IST) continue to apply. After-hours coverage remains Critical issues only.

IT Policy Addendum, October 2026 > 3. Laptop refresh cycle for Engineering (effective 1 January 2027)

The refresh cycle for **Engineering** laptops changes from 4 years to **3 years**. Other roles remain on a 4-year cycle. Engineering laptops already older than 3 years on 1 January 2027 will be replaced in phases through June 2027.

Spotting and Reporting Phishing

# KB-102: Spotting and Reporting Phishing

Spotting and Reporting Phishing > Warning signs

- Urgent language: "act now", "account will be closed", "pay immediately"
- Requests for passwords, one-time codes, or gift cards
- Sender address that looks almost right (for example, `nimbus-logistcs` with a missing letter)
- Unexpected attachments, especially ZIP, HTML, or password-protected files
- Links that do not match the text shown

Spotting and Reporting Phishing > If you receive a suspicious email

1. Do not click links or open attachments.
2. Click the **Report Phish** button in your mail client. If you do not see it, forward the email to `security@nimbus-logistics.example`.
3. Delete it after reporting.

Spotting and Reporting Phishing > If you already clicked

1. Disconnect from Wi-Fi. Do not shut the laptop down.
2. If you entered your password, change it immediately using the self-service reset from another device.
3. Call the Security Hotline at **+91-22-5555-0199**. Do not wait.
4. Write down the time and what you entered or downloaded.

Spotting and Reporting Phishing > Other common scams

- A "CEO" asking for urgent payments or gift cards
- Fake delivery or customs notices
- Requests to "verify" your account on a lookalike login page

IT and Security will never ask you for your password or MFA code.

Working Remotely Securely > Setup checklist

- Use your company laptop, not a personal one
- Connect to the VPN before opening internal systems
- Secure your home Wi-Fi with WPA2 or WPA3 and a strong password
- Work where others cannot see your screen
- Lock your screen whenever you step away

Working Remotely Securely > Public places

Avoid working in cafes, airports, and co-working spaces where possible. If you must, use the VPN and a privacy screen. Never use shared or public computers for work.

Working Remotely Securely > Personal phones

Personal phones can access email, Slack, and calendar once the work profile (MDM) is installed. They must have a screen lock and an up-to-date OS. Rooted or jailbroken devices are not allowed.

Working Remotely Securely > Personal laptops

Personal laptops must not be used to access Confidential or Restricted data.

Working Remotely Securely > Working from abroad

Tell your manager and IT before you travel outside India. Access may be blocked or restricted in some countries.

Working Remotely Securely > Home network tips

- Change the default router admin password
- Keep router firmware updated
- Do not share your work laptop with family members

Data Classification Quick Guide

# KB-105: Data Classification Quick Guide

Data Classification Quick Guide > The four levels

| Level | Examples | Can I email it externally? | Can I store it on my laptop? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Public | Marketing material, job posts | Yes | Yes |
| Internal | Org charts, internal wiki pages | No, unless approved | Yes |
| Confidential | Contracts, pricing, source code | Only with manager approval and encryption | Yes, on encrypted company laptops only |
| Restricted | Customer personal data, credentials, financial records | No | No |

Data Classification Quick Guide > If unsure

Treat the data as the higher level until you confirm with your manager or the Security team.

Data Classification Quick Guide > Sharing files

- Share by link with named people only
- Do not use "anyone with the link" for Internal, Confidential, or Restricted files
- External sharing of Confidential or Restricted files needs manager approval

Data Classification Quick Guide > Using AI tools

Do not paste Confidential or Restricted data into AI tools that are not approved by Nimbus.

Data Classification Quick Guide > Disposal

Shred printed Confidential material. Do not leave printouts on printers or desks.

# IT Quick Tips (v1.2), March 2024

VPN Connection Troubleshooting

# RB-001: VPN Connection Troubleshooting

VPN Connection Troubleshooting > Symptoms

- VPN client shows "Connecting..." and never completes
- Error: "Authentication failed"
- Error: "Gateway unreachable" or timeout
- VPN connects but internal sites (Jira, Confluence) do not load

VPN Connection Troubleshooting > Step 1: Check basic connectivity

1. Open any public website (for example, a search engine). If it does not load, your internet is down; fix that first.
2. If you are on public or hotel Wi-Fi, try a mobile hotspot. Some public networks block VPN traffic.

VPN Connection Troubleshooting > Step 2: Check authentication

1. Confirm your password works by signing in to Nimbus Mail.
2. Approve the MFA prompt promptly. MFA prompts expire after 60 seconds.
3. If you see "Authentication failed" and email works, your VPN certificate may have expired. Go to Step 4.
4. If your account is locked (5 failed attempts), wait 15 minutes or use the self-service reset at `reset.nimbus-logistics.example`.

VPN Connection Troubleshooting > Step 3: Restart the client

1. Fully quit the VPN client (system tray or menu bar icon, then Quit).
2. Reopen it and try again.
3. If it still fails, restart the laptop.

VPN Connection Troubleshooting > Step 4: Reinstall or repair the VPN profile

1. Open the **Software Portal** on your laptop.
2. Select **Nimbus VPN Client** and choose **Repair** (or Reinstall).
3. Sign in again and re-enrol MFA if prompted.

text:
VPN Connection Troubleshooting > Step 5: Connected but internal sites do not load

1. Disconnect and reconnect.
2. Flush DNS:
   - Windows: open Command Prompt and run `ipconfig /flushdns`
   - macOS: run `sudo dscacheutil -flushcache; sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder`
3. Try opening the site by its full address, such as `wiki.nimbus-logistics.example`.
4. Check whether the issue affects one site or all sites. If only one site fails, raise a ticket for that application instead.

metadata.title: VPN Connection Troubleshooting
metadata.section: Step 5: Connected but internal sites do not load
section_path: Step 5: Connected but internal sites do not load

text:
VPN Connection Troubleshooting > When to escalate

Raise a **P3** ticket if steps 1 to 5 do not work. Raise a **P2** ticket if several users in the same office report VPN failure. Attach:

- Screenshot of the error
- Time the issue started
- Your location (home, office, public Wi-Fi)
- Device name (Settings > About)

VPN Connection Troubleshooting > Notes

- Do not disable the VPN to "test" access to internal systems.
- Split tunnelling is not permitted for production access.

- You got a new phone and lost your authenticator app

text:
MFA Lockout and Device Change Recovery > Scenario A: MFA prompts not arriving or codes rejected

1. Check that your phone has internet access and the correct date and time set to **automatic**. One-time codes fail if the phone clock is wrong.
2. Open the authenticator app and check for a pending notification.
3. Try a one-time code instead of push approval, or the other way round.
4. Use your **hardware security key**, if one was issued to you.

If none of these work, move to Scenario B.

text:
MFA Lockout and Device Change Recovery > Scenario B: New phone (old phone still available)

1. On the old phone, open the authenticator app and keep it signed in.
2. On your laptop, go to the security settings page and select **Add a new device**.
3. Scan the QR code with the authenticator app on the new phone.
4. Test a sign-in, then remove the old device.

MFA Lockout and Device Change Recovery > Scenario C: Lost, stolen, or unavailable phone

1. If the phone was lost or stolen, **report it immediately** (see the Incident Reporting section of the handbook). Critical incidents go to the Security Hotline.
2. Contact the IT Service Desk. You must verify your identity before IT can reset MFA:
   - Video call with the Service Desk, showing your company ID badge or government photo ID
   - Or confirmation from your manager through a separate channel
3. IT will reset your MFA enrolment. This takes about 15 minutes after verification.
4. Enrol the new device on first login.
5. Change your password after MFA is reset.

Printer and Scanner Troubleshooting

# RB-003: Printer and Scanner Troubleshooting

Printer and Scanner Troubleshooting > Before you begin

- Printers are available only on the `Nimbus-Corp` Wi-Fi or wired office network.
- Personal devices cannot print to office printers.
- Printers are named by floor and location, for example `MUM-3F-East`.

Printer and Scanner Troubleshooting > Problem: Printer not showing on my laptop

1. Confirm you are connected to `Nimbus-Corp`, not `Nimbus-Guest`.
2. Open the **Software Portal** and search for the printer by name.
3. Select **Install**. Wait for the confirmation message.
4. Print a test page.

metadata.title: Printer and Scanner Troubleshooting
metadata.section: Problem: Printer not showing on my laptop
section_path: Problem: Printer not showing on my laptop

text:
Printer and Scanner Troubleshooting > Problem: Job sent but nothing prints

1. Open the print queue on your laptop and check for stuck jobs. Cancel stuck jobs and resend.
2. Walk to the printer and check for error lights, paper jams, or low toner messages.
3. If the printer uses **secure release**, tap your ID badge on the reader to release the job.
4. Try another printer on the same floor.

metadata.title: Printer and Scanner Troubleshooting

text:
Printer and Scanner Troubleshooting > Problem: Paper jam

1. Open the printer panels shown on the display.
2. Remove the jammed paper gently in the direction of the paper path.
3. Check for torn pieces left inside.
4. Close all panels and wait for the printer to reset.

Printer and Scanner Troubleshooting > Problem: Toner or paper supply

- Paper: refill from the supply cabinet on each floor.
- Toner: raise a **P4** ticket. Do not open toner compartments yourself on multifunction devices.

Printer and Scanner Troubleshooting > Problem: Scan to email not working

1. Confirm the email address on the printer panel is your company address.
2. Files larger than 25 MB cannot be scanned to email. Use scan to cloud drive instead.

Printer and Scanner Troubleshooting > Escalate when

- The error code persists after a restart
- More than 3 users on the same floor cannot print (raise **P2**)
- The printer makes grinding noises or smells of burning (stop using it and raise **P2**)

Warehouse label printers (`Nimbus-IoT` network) are managed by IT. Do not reconfigure them yourself.

Lost or Stolen Device Response

# RB-004: Lost or Stolen Device Response

Lost or Stolen Device Response > Employee actions (first 60 minutes)

1. **Call the Security Hotline: +91-22-5555-0199** (24x7) immediately. Report within 1 hour of noticing the loss.
2. Tell the agent:
   - Device type and asset tag (if known)
   - When and where it was last seen
   - Whether it was locked and powered off
   - What data it may have held
3. If the device was stolen, file a police complaint and keep the reference number. Share it with the Security team.
4. Do not try to track or retrieve the device yourself.

Lost or Stolen Device Response > What Security and IT will do

| Action | Owner | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| Disable the user's sessions and tokens | Security | Immediately |
| Lock or remotely wipe the device | Endpoint team | Within 1 hour of report |
| Reset the user's password and MFA | Identity team | After the device is secured |
| Check access logs for suspicious activity | Security | Within 24 hours |
| Assess data exposure and notify Legal if required | Security + Legal | Within 24 hours |
| Issue replacement device | End User Computing | Within 1 business day |

metadata.title: Lost or Stolen Device Response
metadata.section: What Security and IT will do
section_path: What Security and IT will do

text:
Lost or Stolen Device Response > BYOD devices

For personal phones with the work profile installed, IT can wipe the **work profile only**. Personal data is not touched.

Lost or Stolen Device Response > Laptop encryption

All company laptops use full-disk encryption. A powered-off, locked laptop is considered lower risk, but it must still be reported.

Lost or Stolen Device Response > Restricted data exposure

If the device may have held Restricted data (customer personal data, credentials, financial records), the incident is treated as **Critical** and Legal is notified.

Lost or Stolen Device Response > No-blame reminder

Nimbus does not penalise good-faith loss reported promptly. Delayed reporting is treated more seriously than the loss itself.

Office Wi-Fi and Network Issues

# RB-005: Office Wi-Fi and Network Issues

Office Wi-Fi and Network Issues > Which network should I use?

| Network | For | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Nimbus-Corp` | Company laptops and approved devices | Certificate-based, no password to type |
| `Nimbus-Guest` | Visitors | Internet only; password changes weekly |
| `Nimbus-IoT` | Scanners and printers | IT managed |

Employees must use `Nimbus-Corp` for work. Do not use `Nimbus-Guest` to reach internal systems.

Office Wi-Fi and Network Issues > Problem: Cannot connect to Nimbus-Corp

1. Turn Wi-Fi off and on.
2. Forget the network and reconnect.
3. Check that your device certificate is valid: open the Software Portal and run **Refresh Device Certificate**.
4. If your laptop was recently re-imaged or you changed your password, restart the laptop.
5. If still failing, raise a **P3** ticket with the device name and location.

Office Wi-Fi and Network Issues > Problem: Connected but slow

1. Run a speed test and note the result.
2. Move closer to an access point or try a different floor or room.
3. Check whether others nearby are affected. If many users are affected, notify `#it-help` on Slack and raise **P2**.
4. Pause large downloads and cloud sync during the test.

Office Wi-Fi and Network Issues > Problem: Wi-Fi drops during video meetings

1. Close unused browser tabs and apps.
2. Turn off your camera if bandwidth is limited.
3. Use a wired connection at your desk if available.

text:
Office Wi-Fi and Network Issues > Problem: Websites blocked

Web filtering blocks categories such as malware, adult content, and file-sharing. Do not try to bypass it. If a legitimate business site is blocked, raise a **P4** request with the URL and justification.

Office Wi-Fi and Network Issues > Do not

- Plug in your own routers, switches, or access points
- Run network scans without authorisation from Security

Slow Laptop Performance > Quick checks (5 minutes)

1. **Restart** the laptop. Many laptops run for weeks without a restart, which causes slowdowns.
2. Close unused applications and browser tabs.
3. Check for pending OS or security updates and install them.
4. Check free disk space. Performance drops when less than 10% is free.

Slow Laptop Performance > Find what is using resources

**Windows:** Press `Ctrl + Shift + Esc` to open Task Manager. Sort by CPU, Memory, and Disk.
**macOS:** Open Activity Monitor and sort by CPU and Memory.

| Finding | Action |
|---|---|
| Browser using high memory | Close tabs; restart the browser |
| Cloud sync client using high disk | Let it finish; pause if urgent |
| Unknown process using high CPU | Do not end it; raise a ticket with a screenshot |
| Endpoint security scan running | Let it finish, typically under 30 minutes |

Slow Laptop Performance > Free up disk space

- Empty the Recycle Bin or Trash
- Remove old downloads
- Move large files to the company cloud drive
- Use the Software Portal to uninstall unused applications

Slow Laptop Performance > Do not

- Disable antivirus or the endpoint management agent to speed things up
- Install "cleaner" or "optimiser" tools

Slow Laptop Performance > Escalate when

- The laptop is slow even after restart and cleanup
- The fan runs constantly or the device is very hot
- The battery drains very quickly
- It has been more than 4 years since the laptop was issued (eligible for refresh)

Raise a **P3** ticket with the device name, the symptoms, and what you tried.

Password Reset and Account Lockout

# RB-007: Password Reset and Account Lockout

Password Reset and Account Lockout > Self-service reset

1. Go to `reset.nimbus-logistics.example`.
2. Enter your work email.
3. Verify with MFA.
4. Choose a new password that meets the requirements below.

Password Reset and Account Lockout > Password requirements

- Minimum 14 characters
- Passphrases recommended
- Cannot match your last 10 passwords

Password Reset and Account Lockout > Account locked

- After 5 failed sign-ins, the account locks for 15 minutes.
- Wait 15 minutes, or use the self-service reset.
- If you do not know why your account locked, check for old saved passwords on a phone or laptop mail app, which often cause repeated failures.

Password Reset and Account Lockout > Cannot use self-service

Contact the Service Desk if:

- You cannot receive MFA prompts (see RB-002)
- You are a new joiner and your temporary credentials expired
- Your account was disabled after 90 days of inactivity

Identity verification is required before IT resets credentials.

Password Reset and Account Lockout > After a reset

1. Sign out of all devices and sign back in.
2. Update the saved password on your phone mail app and VPN client.
3. Update the password in the company password manager.

Password Reset and Account Lockout > Suspicious lockouts

If your account locks repeatedly and you did not cause it, someone may be trying to guess your password. Report it to `security@nimbus-logistics.example`.

Software Installation and Requests

# RB-008: Software Installation and Requests

Software Installation and Requests > Installing approved software

1. Open the **Software Portal** on your laptop.
2. Search for the application.
3. Select **Install**.
4. Wait for the confirmation. Large applications can take up to 20 minutes.

Software Installation and Requests > Application not listed

1. Raise a **Software Request** in the Service Portal.
2. Provide:
   - Name and version
   - Business reason
   - Number of users
   - Whether it handles customer or company data
3. IT and Security review licensing, cost, and risk. This typically takes 5 business days.
4. You are notified of the decision. Approved software is added to the Software Portal.

Software Installation and Requests > Install fails

| Error | Fix |
|---|---|
| "Insufficient disk space" | Free up space (see RB-006) |
| "Installation blocked by policy" | The app is not approved; raise a Software Request |
| Install stuck at 0% | Restart the laptop and retry |
| "Licence unavailable" | Raise a P4 ticket; the licence pool may be exhausted |

Software Installation and Requests > Not permitted

- Cracked or pirated software
- Remote-access tools not approved by IT
- Cryptocurrency miners
- File-sharing tools outside approved options

Software Installation and Requests > Developers

Engineers may install IDEs, language runtimes, and container tools from approved sources. Open-source packages are scanned in CI before release.

Software Installation and Requests > AI tools

Use only approved AI assistants. Do not paste customer data, credentials, or Confidential code into unapproved tools. See the AI Usage Guideline on Confluence.
